context.text: What categories of personal data does your organization collect?
What is your primary mechanism for collecting personal data?
Do you use third-party data processors or SaaS vendors who handle personal data on your behalf?
Do you transfer personal data across international borders?
If yes, which regions do you transfer data to?
Do you have a dedicated privacy or Data Protection Officer function?
Do you have an existing information security program?
Have you undergone any privacy or security audit in the past 2 years?
Do you have a documented privacy policy published to users?
Which of the following apply to your organization?
Roughly how many data principals (individuals whose data you hold) are affected?
In the last 2 years, have you experienced any data breach or security incident?
What is the primary driver for this assessment?
What is your target compliance timeline?
What is your approximate budget band for remediation?

dpdpa.description: Organization obtains consent that is free, specific, informed, unconditional, and unambiguous with a clear affirmative action. Consent request is presented in clear, plain language with specified purpose.
dpdpa.title: Lawful basis for processing with free, specific, informed consent

dpdpa.description: When personal data is processed for multiple purposes, consent is obtained separately for each purpose, allowing the Data Principal to give or withhold consent for each.
dpdpa.title: Itemised consent for multiple purposes

dpdpa.description: Data Principals can withdraw consent with the same ease as giving it. Organization ceases processing upon withdrawal unless retention is required by law.
dpdpa.title: Consent withdrawal mechanism

dpdpa.description: If a Consent Manager is used, it is registered with the Data Protection Board and provides an accessible, transparent platform for managing consent.
dpdpa.title: Consent Manager registration and interoperability

dpdpa.description: Verifiable consent of a parent or lawful guardian is obtained before processing personal data of children (under 18) or persons with disabilities.
dpdpa.title: Verifiable parental consent for children's data

dpdpa.description: A clear notice is given to the Data Principal at or before the time of collection, describing the personal data being collected and the purpose of processing.
dpdpa.title: Notice at or before collection of personal data

dpdpa.description: For personal data collected before the Act, a notice is provided as soon as reasonably practicable describing the data held and the processing purposes.
dpdpa.title: Notice for previously collected data

dpdpa.description: The notice includes contact information for the Data Protection Officer or person responsible for addressing Data Principal queries.
dpdpa.title: Notice contains contact details of DPO or grievance officer

dpdpa.description: Personal data is processed only for the purpose for which consent was given or which is deemed legitimate under the Act.
dpdpa.title: Processing only for stated purpose

dpdpa.description: Where processing occurs without consent (Section 7 — voluntary provision, state functions, employment, etc.), the legitimate use basis is documented and appropriate.
dpdpa.title: Legitimate uses without consent properly identified

dpdpa.description: Only personal data that is necessary for the specified purpose is collected. No excessive or irrelevant data is gathered.
dpdpa.title: Collection limited to what is necessary

dpdpa.description: Personal data is erased when the purpose for which it was collected is no longer being served and retention is not necessary for legal purposes.
dpdpa.title: Data retention limited to purpose fulfilment

dpdpa.description: Organization maintains documented retention schedules and automated or systematic procedures for erasing personal data upon purpose completion or consent withdrawal.
dpdpa.title: Retention schedule and deletion procedures

dpdpa.description: Organization makes reasonable efforts to ensure that personal data is complete, accurate, and not misleading, especially where data is used for decisions affecting the Data Principal or shared with other Fiduciaries.
dpdpa.title: Reasonable efforts to ensure data accuracy

dpdpa.description: Organization implements reasonable security safeguards to protect personal data, including prevention of personal data breaches. This includes technical and organizational measures.
dpdpa.title: Reasonable security safeguards implemented

dpdpa.description: Personal data is encrypted at rest and in transit. Access controls ensure only authorized personnel can access personal data based on the principle of least privilege.
dpdpa.title: Encryption and access controls

dpdpa.description: When engaging a Data Processor, the organization has a valid contract ensuring the Processor implements appropriate security safeguards and processes data only as instructed.
dpdpa.title: Data Processor contractual safeguards

dpdpa.description: Data Principals can obtain a summary of their personal data being processed and the processing activities undertaken, including identities of other Fiduciaries and Processors with whom data has been shared.
dpdpa.title: Summary of personal data and processing activities

dpdpa.description: Data Principals can request correction of inaccurate or misleading personal data and completion of incomplete data.
dpdpa.title: Mechanism for correction and completion of data

dpdpa.description: Data Principals can request erasure of personal data that is no longer necessary for the purpose for which it was collected.
dpdpa.title: Mechanism for erasure of personal data

dpdpa.description: Organization provides an accessible mechanism for Data Principals to register grievances. A designated person or officer handles these grievances.
dpdpa.title: Grievance redressal mechanism available

dpdpa.description: Grievances are responded to within a reasonable timeframe. If unresolved, Data Principals are informed of their right to approach the Data Protection Board.
dpdpa.title: Timely response to grievances

dpdpa.description: Data Principals can nominate another individual to exercise their rights in the event of death or incapacity.
dpdpa.title: Nomination mechanism for death or incapacity

dpdpa.description: Organization does not undertake tracking, behavioural monitoring, or targeted advertising directed at children.
dpdpa.title: No tracking or behavioural monitoring of children

dpdpa.description: Processing of children's personal data does not have a detrimental effect on their well-being.
dpdpa.title: No processing detrimental to child's well-being

dpdpa.description: Organization has mechanisms to verify the age of users and identify children to apply appropriate protections and obtain parental consent.
dpdpa.title: Age verification mechanism

dpdpa.description: If designated as a Significant Data Fiduciary, a Data Protection Officer based in India has been appointed who represents the organization to the Board and Data Principals.
dpdpa.title: Data Protection Officer (DPO) appointed

dpdpa.description: An independent Data Auditor has been appointed to evaluate compliance with the Act.
dpdpa.title: Independent Data Auditor appointed

dpdpa.description: Periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments are conducted to evaluate processing activities and associated risks to Data Principals.
dpdpa.title: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) conducted

dpdpa.description: Periodic audits of data processing activities and compliance posture are conducted as prescribed.
dpdpa.title: Periodic audit completed

dpdpa.description: Organization maintains auditable records of when, how, and for what purpose consent was obtained from each Data Principal.
dpdpa.title: Consent records maintained

dpdpa.description: Organization has a process to refresh or re-obtain consent when purposes change or after a reasonable period.
dpdpa.title: Consent refresh and re-validation process

dpdpa.description: Data Principals can provide or withhold consent at a granular level (per-purpose) rather than being forced into all-or-nothing consent.
dpdpa.title: Granular consent options available

dpdpa.description: Access to services is not conditional on consent to processing that is not necessary for the service. No dark patterns used in consent collection.
dpdpa.title: No consent bundling with service access

dpdpa.description: Personal data is transferred outside India only to countries or territories not restricted by the Central Government. Organization maintains an inventory of cross-border data flows.
dpdpa.title: Data transfers only to non-restricted jurisdictions

dpdpa.description: Appropriate contractual or legal safeguards are in place for data transferred outside India, including obligations on the receiving party.
dpdpa.title: Contractual safeguards for cross-border transfers

dpdpa.description: Where the Central Government mandates that certain categories of personal data must be stored in India, the organization complies with such localisation requirements.
dpdpa.title: Data localisation where required

dpdpa.description: Organization has procedures to notify the Data Protection Board of India of any personal data breach in the prescribed form and manner.
dpdpa.title: Breach notification to Data Protection Board

dpdpa.description: Organization has procedures to notify affected Data Principals of a personal data breach in the prescribed form and manner.
dpdpa.title: Breach notification to affected Data Principals

dpdpa.description: A documented incident response plan exists covering detection, containment, investigation, notification, and remediation of personal data breaches.
dpdpa.title: Incident response plan documented

dpdpa.description: Organization maintains a register of all personal data breaches including facts, effects, and remedial actions taken.
dpdpa.title: Breach register maintained

iso27001.description: A set of policies for information security shall be defined, approved by management, published, communicated to and acknowledged by relevant personnel and relevant interested parties.
iso27001.title: Policies for information security

iso27001.description: Information security roles and responsibilities shall be defined and allocated.
iso27001.title: Information security roles and responsibilities

iso27001.description: Conflicting duties and areas of responsibility shall be segregated.
iso27001.title: Segregation of duties

iso27001.description: Management shall require all personnel to apply information security in accordance with the established policies and procedures.
iso27001.title: Management responsibilities

iso27001.description: Appropriate contacts with relevant authorities shall be maintained.
iso27001.title: Contact with authorities

iso27001.description: Appropriate contacts with special interest groups or other specialist security forums shall be maintained.
iso27001.title: Contact with special interest groups

iso27001.description: Information relating to information security threats shall be collected and analysed to produce threat intelligence.
iso27001.title: Threat intelligence

iso27001.description: Information security shall be integrated into project management.
iso27001.title: Information security in project management

iso27001.description: An inventory of information and other associated assets shall be identified and maintained.
iso27001.title: Inventory of information and other associated assets

iso27001.description: Rules for acceptable use and procedures for handling of information and other associated assets shall be identified, documented and implemented.
iso27001.title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets

iso27001.description: Personnel and other interested parties shall return all organizational assets in their possession upon change or termination of employment, contract or agreement.
iso27001.title: Return of assets

iso27001.description: Information shall be classified according to the information security needs of the organization based on confidentiality, integrity, availability and relevant interested party requirements.
iso27001.title: Classification of information

iso27001.description: An appropriate set of procedures for information labelling shall be developed and implemented in accordance with the classification scheme.
iso27001.title: Labelling of information

iso27001.description: Information transfer rules, procedures or agreements shall be in place for all types of transfer facilities.
iso27001.title: Information transfer

iso27001.description: Rules to control physical and logical access to information and other associated assets shall be established and implemented based on business and information security requirements.
iso27001.title: Access control

iso27001.description: The full life cycle of identities shall be managed.
iso27001.title: Identity management

iso27001.description: Allocation and management of authentication information shall be controlled by a management process including advising personnel of appropriate handling.
iso27001.title: Authentication information

iso27001.description: Access rights to information and other associated assets shall be provisioned, reviewed, modified and removed in accordance with the topic-specific policy and rules.
iso27001.title: Access rights

iso27001.description: Processes and procedures shall be defined and implemented to manage the information security risks associated with the use of supplier's products or services.
iso27001.title: Information security in supplier relationships

iso27001.description: Relevant information security requirements shall be established and agreed with each supplier based on the type of supplier relationship.
iso27001.title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements

iso27001.description: Processes and procedures shall be defined and implemented for managing information security risks associated with the ICT products and services supply chain.
iso27001.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain

iso27001.description: The organization shall regularly monitor, review, evaluate and manage change in supplier information security practices and service delivery.
iso27001.title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services

iso27001.description: Processes for acquisition, use, management and exit from cloud services shall be established in accordance with the organization's information security requirements.
iso27001.title: Information security for use of cloud services

iso27001.description: The organization shall plan and prepare for managing information security incidents by defining, establishing and communicating incident management processes, roles and responsibilities.
iso27001.title: Information security incident management planning and preparation

iso27001.description: The organization shall assess information security events and decide if they are to be categorized as information security incidents.
iso27001.title: Assessment and decision on information security events

iso27001.description: Information security incidents shall be responded to in accordance with the documented procedures.
iso27001.title: Response to information security incidents

iso27001.description: Knowledge gained from information security incidents shall be used to strengthen and improve the information security controls.
iso27001.title: Learning from information security incidents

iso27001.description: The organization shall establish and implement procedures for the identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of evidence related to information security events.
iso27001.title: Collection of evidence

iso27001.description: The organization shall plan how to maintain information security at an appropriate level during disruption.
iso27001.title: Information security during disruption

iso27001.description: ICT readiness shall be planned, implemented, maintained and tested based on business continuity objectives and ICT continuity requirements.
iso27001.title: ICT readiness for business continuity

iso27001.description: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements relevant to information security and the organization's approach to meet these requirements shall be identified, documented and kept up to date.
iso27001.title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements

iso27001.description: The organization shall implement appropriate procedures to protect intellectual property rights.
iso27001.title: Intellectual property rights

iso27001.description: Records shall be protected from loss, destruction, falsification, unauthorized access and unauthorized release.
iso27001.title: Protection of records

iso27001.description: The organization shall identify and meet requirements regarding the preservation of privacy and protection of PII as applicable.
iso27001.title: Privacy and protection of personal information

iso27001.description: The organization's approach to managing information security shall be independently reviewed at planned intervals or when significant changes occur.
iso27001.title: Independent review of information security

iso27001.description: Compliance with the organization's information security policy, topic-specific policies, rules and standards shall be regularly reviewed.
iso27001.title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards

iso27001.description: Operating procedures for information processing facilities shall be documented and made available to personnel who need them.
iso27001.title: Documented operating procedures

iso27001.description: Background verification checks on all candidates to become personnel shall be carried out prior to joining the organization and on an ongoing basis.
iso27001.title: Screening

iso27001.description: Employment contractual agreements shall state the personnel's and the organization's responsibilities for information security.
iso27001.title: Terms and conditions of employment

iso27001.description: Personnel and relevant interested parties shall receive appropriate information security awareness, education and training and regular updates of the organization's policies and procedures.
iso27001.title: Information security awareness, education and training

iso27001.description: A disciplinary process shall be formalized and communicated to take actions against personnel who have committed an information security policy violation.
iso27001.title: Disciplinary process

iso27001.description: Information security responsibilities that remain valid after termination or change of employment shall be defined, enforced and communicated.
iso27001.title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment

iso27001.description: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements reflecting the organization's needs for information protection shall be identified, documented, regularly reviewed and signed by personnel and relevant interested parties.
iso27001.title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements

iso27001.description: Security measures shall be implemented when personnel are working remotely to protect information accessed, processed or stored outside the organization's premises.
iso27001.title: Remote working

iso27001.description: The organization shall provide a mechanism for personnel to report observed or suspected information security events through appropriate channels in a timely manner.
iso27001.title: Information security event reporting

iso27001.description: Security perimeters shall be defined and used to protect areas that contain information and other associated assets.
iso27001.title: Physical security perimeters

iso27001.description: Secure areas shall be protected by appropriate entry controls and access points.
iso27001.title: Physical entry

iso27001.description: Physical security for offices, rooms and facilities shall be designed and implemented.
iso27001.title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities

iso27001.description: Premises shall be continuously monitored for unauthorized physical access.
iso27001.title: Physical security monitoring

iso27001.description: Protection against physical and environmental threats shall be designed and implemented.
iso27001.title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats

iso27001.description: Security measures for working in secure areas shall be designed and implemented.
iso27001.title: Working in secure areas

iso27001.description: Clear desk rules for papers and removable storage media and clear screen rules for information processing facilities shall be defined and appropriately enforced.
iso27001.title: Clear desk and clear screen

iso27001.description: Equipment shall be sited securely and protected.
iso27001.title: Equipment siting and protection

iso27001.description: Off-site assets shall be protected.
iso27001.title: Security of assets off-premises

iso27001.description: Storage media shall be managed through their life cycle of acquisition, use, transportation and disposal in accordance with the classification scheme and handling requirements.
iso27001.title: Storage media

iso27001.description: Information processing facilities shall be protected from power failures and other disruptions caused by failures in supporting utilities.
iso27001.title: Supporting utilities

iso27001.description: Cables carrying power, data or supporting information services shall be protected from interception, interference or damage.
iso27001.title: Cabling security

iso27001.description: Equipment shall be maintained correctly to ensure availability, integrity and confidentiality of information.
iso27001.title: Equipment maintenance

iso27001.description: Items of equipment containing storage media shall be verified to ensure that any sensitive data and licensed software has been removed or securely overwritten prior to disposal or re-use.
iso27001.title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment

iso27001.description: Information stored on, processed by or accessible via user endpoint devices shall be protected.
iso27001.title: User endpoint devices

iso27001.description: The allocation and use of privileged access rights shall be restricted and managed.
iso27001.title: Privileged access rights

iso27001.description: Access to information and other associated assets shall be restricted in accordance with the established topic-specific policy on access control.
iso27001.title: Information access restriction

iso27001.description: Read and write access to source code, development tools and software libraries shall be appropriately managed.
iso27001.title: Access to source code

iso27001.description: Secure authentication technologies and procedures shall be established and implemented based on information access restrictions and the topic-specific policy on access control.
iso27001.title: Secure authentication

iso27001.description: The use of resources shall be monitored and adjusted in line with current and expected capacity requirements.
iso27001.title: Capacity management

iso27001.description: Protection against malware shall be implemented and supported by appropriate user awareness.
iso27001.title: Protection against malware

iso27001.description: Information about technical vulnerabilities of information systems in use shall be obtained, the organization's exposure to such vulnerabilities shall be evaluated and appropriate measures shall be taken.
iso27001.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities

iso27001.description: Configurations, including security configurations, of hardware, software, services and networks shall be established, documented, implemented, monitored and reviewed.
iso27001.title: Configuration management

iso27001.description: Information stored in information systems, devices or in any other storage media shall be deleted when no longer required.
iso27001.title: Information deletion

iso27001.description: Data masking shall be used in accordance with the organization's topic-specific policy on access control and other related policies and business requirements, taking applicable legislation into consideration.
iso27001.title: Data masking

iso27001.description: Data leakage prevention measures shall be applied to systems, networks and any other devices that process, store or transmit sensitive information.
iso27001.title: Data leakage prevention

iso27001.description: Backup copies of information, software and systems shall be maintained and regularly tested in accordance with the agreed topic-specific policy on backup.
iso27001.title: Information backup

iso27001.description: Information processing facilities shall be implemented with redundancy sufficient to meet availability requirements.
iso27001.title: Redundancy of information processing facilities

iso27001.description: Logs that record activities, exceptions, faults and other relevant events shall be produced, stored, protected and analysed.
iso27001.title: Logging

iso27001.description: Networks, systems and applications shall be monitored for anomalous behaviour and appropriate actions taken to evaluate potential information security incidents.
iso27001.title: Monitoring activities

iso27001.description: The clocks of information processing systems used by the organization shall be synchronized to approved time sources.
iso27001.title: Clock synchronization

iso27001.description: The use of utility programs that can be capable of overriding system and application controls shall be restricted and tightly controlled.
iso27001.title: Use of privileged utility programs

iso27001.description: Procedures and measures shall be implemented to securely manage software installation on operational systems.
iso27001.title: Installation of software on operational systems

iso27001.description: Networks and network devices shall be secured, managed and controlled to protect information in systems and applications.
iso27001.title: Networks security

iso27001.description: Security mechanisms, service levels and service requirements of network services shall be identified, implemented and monitored.
iso27001.title: Security of network services

iso27001.description: Groups of information services, users and information systems shall be segregated in the organization's networks.
iso27001.title: Segregation of networks

iso27001.description: Access to external websites shall be managed to reduce exposure to malicious content.
iso27001.title: Web filtering

iso27001.description: Rules for the effective use of cryptography, including cryptographic key management, shall be defined and implemented.
iso27001.title: Use of cryptography

iso27001.description: Rules for the secure development of software and systems shall be established and applied.
iso27001.title: Secure development life cycle

iso27001.description: Information security requirements shall be identified, specified and approved when developing or acquiring applications.
iso27001.title: Application security requirements

iso27001.description: Principles for engineering secure systems shall be established, documented, maintained and applied to any information system development activity.
iso27001.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles

iso27001.description: Secure coding principles shall be applied to software development.
iso27001.title: Secure coding

iso27001.description: Security testing processes shall be defined and implemented in the development life cycle.
iso27001.title: Security testing in development and acceptance

iso27001.description: The organization shall direct, monitor and review the activities related to outsourced system development.
iso27001.title: Outsourced development

iso27001.description: Development, testing and production environments shall be separated and secured.
iso27001.title: Separation of development, test and production environments

iso27001.description: Changes to information processing facilities and information systems shall be subject to change management procedures.
iso27001.title: Change management

iso27001.description: Test information shall be appropriately selected, protected and managed.
iso27001.title: Test information

iso27001.description: Audit tests and other assurance activities involving assessment of operational systems shall be planned and agreed between the tester and appropriate management.
iso27001.title: Protection of information systems during audit testing

nist_csf.description: The organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management.
nist_csf.title: Organizational mission understanding

nist_csf.description: Internal and external stakeholders are determined, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood.
nist_csf.title: Internal and external stakeholders

nist_csf.description: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity — including privacy and civil liberties obligations — are understood and managed.
nist_csf.title: Legal and regulatory requirements

nist_csf.description: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that stakeholders depend on or expect are determined and communicated.
nist_csf.title: Critical objectives and dependencies

nist_csf.description: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are determined and prioritized.
nist_csf.title: Outcomes and priorities

nist_csf.description: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders.
nist_csf.title: Risk management objectives

nist_csf.description: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained.
nist_csf.title: Risk appetite and tolerance

nist_csf.description: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes.
nist_csf.title: Risk management activities

nist_csf.description: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated.
nist_csf.title: Strategic risk direction

nist_csf.description: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture of cybersecurity risk awareness.
nist_csf.title: Organizational leadership responsibility

nist_csf.description: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced.
nist_csf.title: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities

nist_csf.description: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies.
nist_csf.title: Adequate resourcing

nist_csf.description: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices.
nist_csf.title: Cybersecurity in HR practices

nist_csf.description: A policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced.
nist_csf.title: Cybersecurity policy

nist_csf.description: Policy is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organizational mission.
nist_csf.title: Policy review and update

nist_csf.description: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction.
nist_csf.title: Risk management strategy review

nist_csf.description: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organizational requirements and risks.
nist_csf.title: Risk management performance

nist_csf.description: Organizational cybersecurity risk management is improved based on lessons learned and assessments.
nist_csf.title: Organizational risk management adjustments

nist_csf.description: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders.
nist_csf.title: Supply chain risk management program

nist_csf.description: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally.
nist_csf.title: Supplier cybersecurity requirements

nist_csf.description: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment, and improvement processes.
nist_csf.title: Supply chain integration

nist_csf.description: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality.
nist_csf.title: Supplier assessment

nist_csf.description: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other types of agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties.
nist_csf.title: Supply chain requirements in contracts

nist_csf.description: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained.
nist_csf.title: Hardware asset inventory

nist_csf.description: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained.
nist_csf.title: Software asset inventory

nist_csf.description: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained.
nist_csf.title: Network communication mapping

nist_csf.description: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained.
nist_csf.title: External service inventory

nist_csf.description: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission.
nist_csf.title: Asset prioritization

nist_csf.description: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained.
nist_csf.title: Data inventory and classification

nist_csf.description: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles.
nist_csf.title: Systems and services in scope

nist_csf.description: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded.
nist_csf.title: Vulnerability identification

nist_csf.description: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources.
nist_csf.title: Threat intelligence receipt

nist_csf.description: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded.
nist_csf.title: Threat identification

nist_csf.description: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded.
nist_csf.title: Impact and likelihood assessment

nist_csf.description: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization.
nist_csf.title: Risk determination

nist_csf.description: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated.
nist_csf.title: Risk response selection

nist_csf.description: Improvements are identified from evaluations.
nist_csf.title: Improvement from evaluations

nist_csf.description: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties.
nist_csf.title: Improvement from testing

nist_csf.description: Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities.
nist_csf.title: Improvement from execution

nist_csf.description: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization.
nist_csf.title: Identity and credential management

nist_csf.description: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions.
nist_csf.title: Identity proofing

nist_csf.description: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated.
nist_csf.title: Authentication

nist_csf.description: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified.
nist_csf.title: Identity assertions

nist_csf.description: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties.
nist_csf.title: Access permissions and authorizations

nist_csf.description: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk.
nist_csf.title: Physical access management

nist_csf.description: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind.
nist_csf.title: Security awareness

nist_csf.description: Individuals in specialized roles are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform relevant tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind.
nist_csf.title: Privileged user training

nist_csf.description: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected.
nist_csf.title: Data-at-rest protection

nist_csf.description: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected.
nist_csf.title: Data-in-transit protection

nist_csf.description: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected.
nist_csf.title: Data-in-use protection

nist_csf.description: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested.
nist_csf.title: Backup management

nist_csf.description: The configuration of network infrastructure is established, applied, and reviewed incorporating security principles.
nist_csf.title: Configuration management practices

nist_csf.description: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk.
nist_csf.title: Software maintenance

nist_csf.description: Hardware is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk.
nist_csf.title: Hardware maintenance

nist_csf.description: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring.
nist_csf.title: Log record generation

nist_csf.description: Installation and execution of unauthorized software is prevented.
nist_csf.title: Installation and execution prevention

nist_csf.description: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle.
nist_csf.title: Secure software development

nist_csf.description: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage.
nist_csf.title: Network and environment protection

nist_csf.description: The organization's technology assets are protected from environmental threats.
nist_csf.title: Technology asset protection

nist_csf.description: Mechanisms are implemented to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations.
nist_csf.title: Resilience mechanisms

nist_csf.description: Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained.
nist_csf.title: Adequate resource capacity

nist_csf.description: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
nist_csf.title: Network monitoring

nist_csf.description: The physical environment is monitored to find potentially adverse events.
nist_csf.title: Physical environment monitoring

nist_csf.description: Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
nist_csf.title: Personnel activity monitoring

nist_csf.description: External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
nist_csf.title: External service provider monitoring

nist_csf.description: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
nist_csf.title: Computing hardware and software monitoring

nist_csf.description: Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities.
nist_csf.title: Event correlation

nist_csf.description: Information is correlated from multiple sources.
nist_csf.title: Event aggregation

nist_csf.description: The estimated impact and scope of adverse events are understood.
nist_csf.title: Impact estimation

nist_csf.description: Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools.
nist_csf.title: Incident declaration

nist_csf.description: Cyber threat intelligence and other contextual information are integrated into the analysis.
nist_csf.title: Threat information integration

nist_csf.description: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria.
nist_csf.title: Anomaly detection

nist_csf.description: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared.
nist_csf.title: Incident response plan execution

nist_csf.description: Incident reports are triaged and validated.
nist_csf.title: Incident triage and prioritization

nist_csf.description: Incidents are categorized and prioritized.
nist_csf.title: Incident categorization and prioritization

nist_csf.description: Incidents are escalated or elevated as needed.
nist_csf.title: Incident escalation

nist_csf.description: The criteria for initiating incident recovery are applied.
nist_csf.title: Incident criteria application

nist_csf.description: Analysis is performed to determine what has taken place during an incident and the root cause of the incident.
nist_csf.title: Root cause analysis

nist_csf.description: Actions performed during an investigation are recorded, and the records' integrity and provenance are preserved.
nist_csf.title: Investigation actions

nist_csf.description: Incident data and metadata are collected and their integrity and provenance are preserved.
nist_csf.title: Incident data collection and analysis

nist_csf.description: An incident's magnitude is estimated and validated.
nist_csf.title: Incident scope estimation

nist_csf.description: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents.
nist_csf.title: Internal stakeholder notification

nist_csf.description: Information is shared with designated internal and external stakeholders.
nist_csf.title: Incident information sharing

nist_csf.description: Incident information is shared with designees consistent with response plans and information sharing agreements.
nist_csf.title: Voluntary incident information sharing

nist_csf.description: Incidents are contained.
nist_csf.title: Incident containment

nist_csf.description: Incidents are eradicated.
nist_csf.title: Incident eradication

nist_csf.description: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated from the incident response process.
nist_csf.title: Recovery plan execution

nist_csf.description: Recovery actions are selected, scoped, prioritized, and performed.
nist_csf.title: Recovery action selection

nist_csf.description: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration.
nist_csf.title: Recovery verification

nist_csf.description: Critical mission functions and cybersecurity risk management are considered to establish post-incident operational norms.
nist_csf.title: Mission function consideration

nist_csf.description: The integrity of restored assets is verified, systems and services are restored, and normal operating status is confirmed.
nist_csf.title: Recovery completeness verification

nist_csf.description: The end of incident recovery is declared based on criteria, and incident-related documentation is completed.
nist_csf.title: End of recovery declaration

nist_csf.description: Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders.
nist_csf.title: Recovery activity communication

nist_csf.description: Public updates on incident recovery are shared using approved methods and messaging.
nist_csf.title: Public update communication

iso27001.help_text: Define which parts of the organization, business processes, and information assets are within scope.
iso27001.text: What is the scope of your Information Security Management System (ISMS)?

iso27001.help_text: Cloud services include IaaS, PaaS and SaaS (including email and file sharing). If you answer No, the cloud-services control (A.5.23) is proposed as likely not applicable for the consultant to confirm; nothing is removed automatically.
iso27001.text: Does your organization use cloud services for storing or processing information?

iso27001.help_text: If you answer No, the development-specific controls (A.8.4, A.8.25, A.8.28, A.8.30, A.8.31, A.8.33) are proposed as likely not applicable; if development is in-house only, outsourced development (A.8.30) is. The consultant confirms each one; nothing is removed automatically.
iso27001.text: Does your organization develop software or systems (in-house or outsourced)?

iso27001.help_text: If you are fully remote with no premises, the site-related physical controls (A.7.1-A.7.6, A.7.8, A.7.11, A.7.12) are proposed as likely not applicable for the consultant to confirm. Controls that still apply to remote staff and equipment (A.7.7, A.7.9, A.7.10, A.7.13, A.7.14) stay in scope.

options.label: Yes — including data center / server room

iso27001.text: Does your organization have physical premises with sensitive information processing facilities?

nist_csf.help_text: NIST CSF was originally developed for critical infrastructure sectors. Recorded as context for the consultant; it does not change which CSF outcomes are assessed.

options.label: Yes — but CSF adoption is voluntary

nist_csf.text: Is your organization part of critical infrastructure (e.g., energy, healthcare, financial services, transportation)?

nist_csf.help_text: CSF 2.0 defines 4 tiers: Partial (Tier 1), Risk Informed (Tier 2), Repeatable (Tier 3), Adaptive (Tier 4). Recorded as your self-assessed starting point for the consultant; it does not change which outcomes are assessed or how they are scored.

options.label: Tier 2 — Risk Informed (some risk awareness, not org-wide)

nist_csf.text: What is your organization's current CSF implementation tier?

nist_csf.help_text: OT/ICS environments have unique cybersecurity considerations. Recorded as context for the consultant; the CSF outcomes in this assessment are not OT-specific and all remain in scope.
nist_csf.text: Does your organization manage operational technology (OT) or industrial control systems (ICS)?

nist_csf.help_text: A CSF profile aligns framework outcomes with business requirements, risk tolerance, and resources.

options.label: Yes — both current and target profiles

nist_csf.text: Has your organization developed a CSF organizational profile (current or target)?
